design.hypothesis: A viscosity proxy built from about 1 ns of LOPLS-AA molecular dynamics at 40 °C (313.15 K) ranks the 8 benchmark molecules like their reference viscosities. The proxy is kT/(6π·D·R). D is the self-diffusion coefficient from mean-squared displacement of molecular centres. R is a radius from the simulated density and molar mass. The claim is Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.8, stable across replicas, cheaper than the paper's Green-Kubo runs, working inside chemical families, and better than free orderings.
models: Force field: LOPLS-AA (a long-chain variant of the OPLS all-atom force field), built with the committed SMILES-to-LAMMPS builder after a line-by-line review. The builder and decks are untrusted until reviewed.
Engine: LAMMPS with GPU acceleration on one rented single-GPU box (GUESS: LAMMPS GPU package is installed and works on the box; if not, OpenMM from pip is the fallback, and the fallback is recorded).
Comparison ordering only, no new training: released out-of-fold XGBoost-descriptor viscosity predictions at 40 °C (column xgboost_descriptors_40C, rho about 0.738 as stated in the question).
No language models, no layers, no steering strengths. Those fields do not apply.

arms: Main proxy (Stokes-Einstein-like): per molecule, kT/(6π·D·R), D averaged over 3 replicas of about 1 ns production. R=(3M/(4πρN_A))^(1/3) from the simulated density. Judged against reference viscosity at 40 °C.
Control, diffusion only: 1/D with no size term. Shows whether the size term helps.
Control, simulated density only: MD density from the same runs as a ranking. Shows whether the proxy beats the density that equilibration gives for free.
Control, free orderings (no MD): molar mass, reference density, and released XGBoost out-of-fold predictions, each used directly as a ranking.
Control, chance: exact distribution of Spearman rho over all 40320 orderings of 8 items. Gives the probability that a random ordering reaches rho of at least 0.8.
Control, planted known truth: synthetic trajectories with known D, plus a synthetic known-order and reversed-order pair, to prove the code recovers D and returns rho of +1 and -1.

Validation arm, long run: replica 1 of each molecule continued for 5 ns more in constant volume (GUESS: 5 ns is long enough to be diffusive for squalane). Gives a longer-trajectory D for the same systems.
Replica arm: the 3 independent 1-ns runs scored separately, to measure rerun dispersion and ordering stability.
Density reproduction arm: first number to reproduce, simulated 40 °C density against the paper's value for each molecule, before any proxy is trusted.

endpoints.metric: Density gate. Per molecule, simulated 40 °C density (mean of last 0.8 ns of a 1 ns constant-pressure run, 3 replicas) relative to the paper's MD density. Tetraethylene glycol diethyl ether must also sit at least 6% below its reference density while the other 7 sit within 4% of reference. Those bands are derived from the paper's own labels: the others are within 3%, the outlier is -10%.
endpoints.threshold: At least 7 of 8 molecules within ±2% of the paper MD density, AND the outlier condition holds. Fewer than 7 passing marks the proxy result uninterpretable, not refuted.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Two or more molecules outside ±2%, or a second molecule beyond 4% of reference, or the glycol ether not low. The systems are not built like the paper's, and the proxy ranking is not judged.

endpoints.metric: MAIN. Spearman rho between the main proxy and the reference 40 °C viscosities of the 8 molecules. Reference order is hexyl-diphenylheptane > squalane > propylheptyl-naphthalene > decyl stearate > sebacate > trioxanonadecane > glycol diethyl ether > nonylcyclohexane. A data-only pre-check confirms this order from dataset.csv and from predictions_viscosity.csv.
endpoints.threshold: rho >= 0.8, equivalent to a sum of squared rank differences <= 16. Below 0.6 is also reported as the reframing step's abandon line.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: rho < 0.8 with the density gate passed. Chance probability of rho >= 0.8 from the exact permutation count is reported beside it.

endpoints.metric: Stability. Pairwise Spearman rho between the 3 replica orderings, and rho between the 1-ns mean ordering and the long-run ordering. Also each replica's own rho against reference, with mean and range reported as rerun dispersion.
endpoints.threshold: All 3 replica-replica rho >= 0.8 and long-run agreement rho >= 0.8. The 0.8 is the question's own bar. Dispersion of exactly zero across replicas halts the run as WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Any replica pair below 0.8, or long-run agreement below 0.8. The ranking then rests on noise.

endpoints.metric: Cost. Simulated nanoseconds per molecule for the proxy: 3 replicas times (1 ns equilibration + 1 ns production). The long run is validation only and is excluded but reported. Paper baseline is 10 replicas times 8 ns = 80 ns per molecule per temperature.
endpoints.threshold: <= 8 ns per molecule, i.e. at most 10% of the paper's simulated time. Measured GPU hours per molecule are also reported. CPU-hours and GPU-hours are not directly comparable, so the ns ratio is the judged number.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: More than 8 ns per molecule, for example if 5 replicas are needed to stabilise the order.

endpoints.metric: Family test. Concordant pairs among the 12 within-group pairs: 6 among the 4 hydrocarbons (alkanes, aromatics) and 6 among the 4 oxygenates (esters, polyethers). A pair is concordant if proxy order equals reference order. Also report the between-group offset as the ratio of group-mean proxy to group-mean reference.
endpoints.threshold: At least 10 of 12 concordant. Derived from the exact binomial: 10 of 12 gives one-sided p = 0.019 under chance, 9 of 12 gives 0.073. Pairs are not independent, so this is approximate.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Fewer than 10 of 12 concordant while the main rho is >= 0.8. The correlation is then carried by hydrocarbon-versus-oxygenate order.

endpoints.metric: Added value. Main-proxy rho minus the largest rho among the free orderings (molar mass, reference density, simulated density, released XGBoost out-of-fold at about 0.738) and the diffusion-only and simulated-density controls.
endpoints.threshold: Main proxy rho strictly greater than every control rho. Rho moves in steps of about 0.012, and with n = 8 differences below 0.05 are reported as ties.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Any control with rho at or above the main proxy, or within 0.05 of it. The result is true but uninformative.

endpoints.metric: Analysis code check on planted data. Recovered D on 20 synthetic ensembles versus true D, and the three outcome labels (pass, refute, non-diffusive) each reached by a planted case.
endpoints.threshold: Mean bias of recovered D within 2 standard errors of the 20 ensembles. Known-order gives rho = +1 and reversed gives -1. A subdiffusive synthetic case must receive the non-diffusive label.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Bias beyond 2 standard errors, or any label unreachable. Real results are not read until fixed.

endpoints.metric: Diffusion fit window rule. On the 2 calibration molecules only, choose the window where the log-log slope of mean-squared displacement against time lies in 0.9 to 1.1 (GUESS band), at least 0.3 ns wide. The same rule is applied unchanged to the 8.
endpoints.threshold: A window of at least 0.3 ns must exist for each of the 8. A molecule without one is labelled non-diffusive in 1 ns and scored from its last 0.5 ns with a flag; the main rho is also reported with it excluded.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Three or more of the 8 labelled non-diffusive. The 1-ns claim is refuted on its own terms, whatever rho shows.

design.sampling: Each box holds about 15,000 atoms (the paper's size). Each replica has an independent packing seed and velocity seed; seeds are 11, 22 and 33 (GUESS, arbitrary labels). Equilibration: 1 ns at constant pressure (1 atm) and 313.15 K with the committed deck's thermostat and barostat after review. Production: 1 ns at constant volume, set to the equilibrated mean box, same temperature, with the deck's timestep (GUESS: 1 to 2 fs). Molecular centre-of-mass positions are written unwrapped every 1 ps. Overall drift is removed. Mean-squared displacement uses all time origins. D is the slope divided by 6 over the fit window. Cells: 8 molecules times 3 replicas for the proxy; 8 long runs; 2 calibration molecules with 1 replica each. Density uses the last 0.8 ns of equilibration. Temperature is 313.15 K only; 100 °C is not run.
does_not_test: Finite-size correction to D. It needs viscosity, which is circular. Box sizes differ by molecule, so D errors could reorder close pairs. How wrong: unknown; shifts could be 10 to 30% in D (GUESS).
Excess-entropy scaling. Only the Stokes-Einstein-like form is judged. If it fails, an entropy form might still pass.
Whether the reference labels are right. Two of eight are PPDS 9 correlations, the sebacate was patched after training, and the glycol ether density looks high. All are taken as given.

Order of the top two molecules (squalane 15.06 and hexyl-diphenylheptane 15.57, 3.4% apart). Their order is within plausible reference error, which is unverified. With n = 8, one swap changes rho by about 0.024.
Any claim at 100 °C, other force fields, thermal conductivity, or the 835-molecule set. Eight molecules cannot support a general claim.
Absolute viscosity accuracy; only rank is asked.
GUESS: throughput of 25 ns/day for 15,000 atoms on one GPU. If it is 10 ns/day, cost rises to about $330 and the long runs are shortened to 2 ns first.
GUESS: box price of $1.5 per hour. Wrong by 2x would move the cost between $100 and $400.
GUESS: total simulated time about 92 ns (48 proxy, 40 long, 4 calibration), 88 GPU hours, plus 50% for setup and reruns.
GUESS: slope band 0.9 to 1.1 and 0.3 ns minimum window. Wrong band could include ballistic or caged motion; the calibration molecules check only two chemistries.
GUESS: 5 ns long run is diffusive for squalane. If not, long-run agreement is itself non-diffusive and the stability endpoint is reported as inconclusive.
GUESS: 3 replicas. With 3, a rho range is a rough dispersion estimate only; no confidence interval is claimed.
MEMORY: the builder emits LAMMPS inputs for LOPLS-AA and the decks run as described in the repo README. Not checked here; review is a required first step.
Spearman rho at n = 8 has coarse steps (about 0.012) and wide uncertainty; one rank swap near the threshold can flip the verdict.
